sources_used.commit: not a git repository; file fingerprinted in index.json

evidence.summary: FAQ is a hard-coded list of question/answer pairs (one entry about password reset).
suggest(text) lower-cases and splits the text on whitespace and returns every FAQ whose question shares at least one word, unranked.

architecture.backend: One Python module with an in-memory FAQ list and a suggest function
architecture.frontend: none in the folder (the user calls it a widget; no widget code present)

features.name: FAQ entries
features.description: A list of frequently asked questions with their answers.
features.observed_behaviour: Static in-code list; no way to add, edit or delete entries at runtime.
features.business_logic: Each entry has q (question) and a (answer).
features.integration: Becomes a stored, editable FAQ entity in the unified app.

features.name: Suggest FAQ answers for text
features.description: Given some text, return the FAQ entries that look relevant.
features.observed_behaviour: Case-insensitive whitespace tokenisation; any shared word matches; no stop-word filtering, punctuation stripping or ranking, so common words like 'how' or 'i' match almost everything and 'password?' does not match 'password'.
features.business_logic: match if |words(text) ∩ words(question)| >= 1; results in list order.
features.integration: Run against ticket text to suggest answers on each ticket.

unknowns: The widget UI the user mentions is not in the folder; only the matching logic was provided.
No persistence, auth or API: how FAQ entries are maintained in practice is unknown.
